chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said: a man from our companions narrated to me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Nine-tenths of livelihood is with the owner of the riding animal.

key_terms.الدابة: The riding animal or beast of burden, particularly camels, mules, or horses used for transport and trade
key_terms.الرزق: Livelihood, sustenance, provision — broadly encompassing all means of earning a living
key_terms.تسعة أعشار: Nine-tenths — an emphatic fraction indicating the overwhelming preponderance of animal-based livelihood

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the role of riding animals in earning a livelihood?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that nine out of ten portions of one's livelihood is obtained through the ownership and use of a riding animal (dabbah). This hadith reflects the agrarian and mercantile economy of early Islamic society, where pack animals — camels, mules, and horses — were essential for transport, trade, agriculture, and travel. The teaching encourages investment in animals as a primary source of wealth and economic activity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from a man from his companions, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Nine-tenths of the livelihood is with the owner of the animal’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jundab has said that narrated to him certain persons of our people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Nine-tenths of sustenance is with the owner of a stumper.’”
